text:
rachel: heads up — tenant-99 onprem-sjc reported a sudden spike of keystore wrap/get calls. Breakglass token appears in the audit :rotating_light:
infra-bot: keystore-monitor alert: breakglass=true; spike=18; window=7m; src_nodes=[sjc-3a,sjc-3b]; reason=auto-failover
omar: affected pods: `kubectl -n priv-keystore get pods -l app=keystore-agent -o name` -> keystore-agent-3a, keystore-agent-3b.
tina: pulling vault audit lines now. snippet:
```
time=2026-03-20T04:12:31Z method=wrap path=/v1/transit/keys/tenant-99 action=wrap auth.token_id=tb-77 role=breakglass auth.method=token
```
omar: token tb-77 was issued to svcacc-failover during a rolling restart job (ci:deploy-runner).
security-bot: flag correlation: ci:deploy-runner triggered rolling restart at 04:09; vault-unseal returned i/o timeout at 04:08 -> migration didn't complete.
rachel: so RBAC hardening (mfa requirement + egress whitelist) didn't land on those nodes. We need to treat this as an availability automation interacting with a stale privileged token.
jonah: triage plan: 1) revoke tb-77 2) rotate breakglass creds 3) snapshot audit/vault logs + netpols/iptables from affected nodes 4) apply RBAC patch as a canary to one pod 5) investigate why migration timed out.
tina: revoking token now: `vault token-revoke tb-77` — done. creating short-lived manual token for ops with TTL=1h.
omar: collecting forensic artifacts: `kubectl -n priv-keystore exec -it keystore-agent-3a -- sh -c "iptables-save > /tmp/iptables.snap; cat /etc/netpols/*.yaml > /tmp/netpols.snap; tar czf /tmp/forensic.tgz /var/log/keystore /var/lib/audit /tmp/iptables.snap /tmp/netpols.snap"` then scp to secure-bucket. upload key: s3://secure-bucket/forensics/1795012345/forensic.tgz
security-bot: also include host dmesg and container maps for crash correlation.
rachel: RBAC patch (Vault policy snippet) we want to push as a canary:
```yaml
path "transit/*" {
  capabilities = ["wrap","read"]
  allowed_params = {
    "auth_method" = ["mfa"]
    "source_ip" = ["10.30.5.0/24"]
  }
}
```
jonah: apply to a single pod: `kubectl apply -f rbac-vault-canary.yaml -n priv-keystore --selector=pod=keystore-agent-3a` then monitor `vault_audit_lines` for denied vs allowed.
tina: migration job logs show `dial tcp 10.8.2.1:8200: i/o timeout` between 04:06-04:09; networking team reports BGP flap in that window.
omar: immediate netpol mitigation: open ephemeral egress from priv-keystore namespace to vault-unseal cluster IP for 15m via canary networkpolicy.
security-bot: add alert: `vault_breakglass_usage > 3 in 5m` to notify eng-security + compliance. Recommend threshold=3 to avoid noise.
rachel: compliance question: do we need to rotate tenant keys used during gap? If audit shows they were only wrapped/unwrapped by internal automation and no external principals, maybe not, but escalate to compliance for decision.
jonah: propose conservative approach: identify keys touched between 03:50-04:20 from vault audit and mark for rotation if any audit buffer gaps exist. Run `vault audit search` and produce list.
tina: assembling list: `key-omega, key-sigma` touched in window. uploading list to incident folder.
security-bot: recommended post-incident fixes: 1) make RBAC migration idempotent and observable with a pre/post check that confirms policy applied 2) add a migration heartbeat check that fails CI if vault-unseal unreachable 3) enforce that automated failover paths do not use long-lived breakglass tokens 4) add audit-forwarder redundancy so logs survive agent crashes.
omar: agree. also suggest we add an early-warning metric for `migration_pending_pods` and a runbook step to pause rolling restarts when control plane connectivity is degraded.
rachel: I've opened the incident doc and assigned owners for revocation, forensic upload, canary RBAC, networking follow-up, and compliance notification. Will schedule a retro with CI team and networking tomorrow.
jonah: all done on revocation and forensic uploads; canary RBAC applied to keystore-agent-3a, watching metrics now.
rachel: thanks everyone. keep this thread updated; we'll close once canary shows no denied legitimate ops and compliance signs off.
